rule.title: ERC4626 withdraw or redeem override burns owner shares and transfers assets without caller authorization

intent.attack_thesis: An ERC4626 vault override of withdraw or redeem directly burns shares from an arbitrary owner parameter and transfers underlying assets to an arbitrary receiver parameter without verifying that the caller is the owner or holds sufficient share allowance. Any external caller can drain any depositor.

flows_all.description: shares burned from owner parameter without caller==owner or allowance gate
underlying assets sent to receiver parameter after burning non-caller's shares

reporting.title_template: ERC4626 vault withdraw/redeem allows unauthorized caller to drain any depositor
reporting.summary: Matches an ERC4626 vault where withdraw() or redeem() overrides burn shares from a calldata-supplied owner and transfer assets to a calldata-supplied receiver without verifying the caller is authorized to act for that owner.
reporting.user_summary: This vault lets anyone call withdraw or redeem with another user's address as the owner. The vault burns that user's shares and sends the underlying tokens to any address the caller chooses. An attacker can drain every depositor's funds in a single transaction.
reporting.technical_summary: The detector identifies ERC4626 vault overrides of withdraw(uint256,address,address) or redeem(uint256,address,address) where the function performs _burn(owner, shares) and safeTransfer(receiver, assets) using calldata parameters, but the execution path contains neither a CALLER==owner equality check nor an allowance SLOAD+comparison before the burn. The standard ERC4626._withdraw() safeguard — if (caller != owner) _spendAllowance(owner, caller, shares) — is absent because the override reimplements the function directly without delegating to the base internal function.
reporting.exploit_narrative: The attacker calls withdraw(victim_balance, attacker_address, victim_address) on the vault. Because the override never checks whether msg.sender is the victim or holds share allowance, the vault reads the victim's deposit info, burns the victim's shares, and sends the underlying USDC to the attacker. The attacker repeats this for each depositor, draining the entire vault. In the YieldCore RWAVault exploit, this pattern was used 8 times in one transaction to steal 392,763 USDC from 8 depositors.
exploit_preconditions: vault inherits ERC4626 but overrides withdraw or redeem at the public function level
override reimplements burn-and-transfer logic without delegating to _withdraw()
override accepts owner as a calldata parameter and uses it for _burn() target
override accepts receiver as a calldata parameter and uses it for asset transfer target
no require(msg.sender == owner) or _spendAllowance check exists on the execution path
remediation_hints: override the internal _withdraw() function instead of the public withdraw()/redeem() functions
if overriding public withdraw/redeem, always include: if (msg.sender != owner) _spendAllowance(owner, msg.sender, shares)
add require(msg.sender == owner || allowance(owner, msg.sender) >= shares) before burning shares
follow OpenZeppelin's documented guidance: override _withdraw() and _deposit(), not the public entry points
add integration tests that verify a non-owner without allowance cannot call withdraw/redeem on behalf of another address

preconditions: withdraw/redeem override is missing allowance check

steps.action: call withdraw/redeem passing victim as owner, attacker as receiver
steps.expected_state: victim shares burned; assets transferred to attacker without allowance

witness_goal.success_condition: attacker drains victim vault shares without authorization
